verdict.rationale: TypeSafe documents a concrete guardrail pattern — the llm_guardrails cookbook screens every message in/out of an LLM app with one API call, thresholding hazard probabilities/severity to pass, review, block, or route — plus a confidence-routing pattern ('confidence tells you whether to act') and a vendor-authored jaggedness page listing nine failure modes with mitigations. However, this is a usage pattern built on general Choice/Score primitives rather than a dedicated moderation/safety endpoint, and a hands-on community critique (jev-comm-7) specifically challenges the reliability of the confidence signal that the gating pattern depends on ('Jev's confidence output is fake/redundant... conveys no additional information'), undercutting trust in the core gating mechanism. Missing for 10: a first-class moderation/safety-classification endpoint distinct from general-purpose Choice/Score, independent validation that the guardrails cookbook pattern works reliably in production, and resolution of the confidence-calibration critique.
